headline: Approved amendments to the 202 Woodford Street housing TIF district, a zoning change for entertainment businesses, and grants for the jetport, historic preservation, and housing programs.
summary: The council approved several orders including a utility easement termination, amendments to the 202 Woodford Street affordable housing TIF district and its credit enhancement agreement, and a zoning amendment for entertainment businesses in the B-3 and WCZ zones. It also accepted and appropriated grant funds for jetport equipment, historic preservation staff support, and housing development, and appointed Robert Foster to the Land Bank Commission. Several other orders, including funding for Hope House rehabilitation and a Department of Transportation agreement, received only a first reading.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of 07.20.2026, 8-0.
Appointed Robert Foster to the Land Bank Commission, 8-0.
Accepted the Portland Public Art Committee Fiscal Year 2026 Annual Report and Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Plan, 8-0.
Approved termination and release of a utility easement between the City of Portland, Loring House Associates Limited Partnership, and the Portland Water District, 8-0.
Approved an amendment to the 202 Woodford Street Affordable Housing Development District and Tax Increment Financing District and adopted the amended Municipal Development Program, 8-0.
Approved an amended Credit Enhancement Agreement for the 202 Woodford Street Affordable Housing and Tax Increment Financing District, 8-0.
Accepted and appropriated $225,000 in FAA, State of Maine, and Jetport matching funds to install ADS-B transponders in 57 airfield vehicles, passed as an emergency, 8-0.
Accepted and appropriated a $25,000 Maine Historic Preservation Commission grant for staff support, passed as an emergency, 8-0.
Accepted and appropriated $10,000 from the State of Maine's Housing Opportunity Program for housing development, passed as an emergency, 7-1 with Councilor Sykes opposed.
Approved an amendment to Portland City Code on entertainment businesses in the B-3 and WCZ zones, passed as an emergency, 8-0.
